title: Energy Kiosk
description: In 2009, e.quinox opened a pilot Energy Kiosk in Rwanda, one of the organisation's first projects on the ground. The trip tested a new technical solution and explored how a sustainable business model could bring reliable electricity to rural communities.
description2: The kiosk was monitored remotely through a custom data-logging system and maintained by Rwandan partners, ensuring it could keep running long after the team returned to London. The project gave e.quinox an early real-world proof of concept and a platform for future work.
outcomes: Early e.quinox installation on the ground
Remote monitoring via a custom data-logging system
Community ownership and maintenance model established

title: Home Lighting
imageAlt: Portable battery boxes distributed in Rwandan homes, 2013
description: In 2013, e.quinox returned to Rwanda to expand its work through a new home lighting initiative. The team worked with local communities to deliver portable battery boxes, giving households access to reliable light and power for the first time.
description2: Alongside this, the team trained and collaborated with local entrepreneurs to manufacture and distribute the systems. The expedition strengthened e.quinox's approach of combining engineering with community-led development, laying a foundation for future projects.
outcomes: Portable battery boxes deployed to homes
Local entrepreneurs trained to manufacture and distribute

title: Rainwater Recon
imageAlt: The 2024 e.quinox team in discussion with partners in Rwanda
description: In 2024, a team returned to Rwanda to study how to improve both the quality and quantity of water access. The work focused on household rainwater harvesting as a scalable, accessible and transportable way to bring water to rural homes.
description2: The team received guidance from Rwanda's Ministry of Infrastructure and worked with the Dean of Engineering at the University of Rwanda. Their feedback shaped the design and engineering choices behind Project Amazi.
outcomes: Household surveys and costings in Gakenke District
Guidance from Rwanda's Ministry of Infrastructure
Collaboration with the University of Rwanda

title: Project Amazi
imageAlt: The first Project Amazi system: tanks on a raised stand beside a home in Minazi Sector, Gakenke District
description: Project Amazi is e.quinox's deployable, modular rainwater harvester for rural Rwandan households. Each 700 L system links several tanks in parallel, so families can add capacity as their needs and means allow. The first system was installed in Minazi Sector in spring 2026 to test deployability, supply chain and yield.
description2: The 2026 business case, written by Riccardo Casonato (Imperial College London), finds Amazi 3.2× cheaper to install and 3.8× cheaper to run than a communal pumped tap from WASAC. It meets over 40% of household water needs nine months a year in every province, even when capturing only half the rain. Every part can be carried by hand, by moto and on public transport, which cuts delivery costs by 90%.
outcomes: First 700 L modular harvester installed in Minazi Sector
Water quality tested with the University of Rwanda
3.2× cheaper to install and 3.8× cheaper to run than a pumped tap
Over 40% of water needs met nine months a year, in every province
Business case developed for stakeholders, after talks with MININFRA

title: Truckle
imageAlt: Truckle prototype build, an earlier e.quinox project
description: Truckle was an earlier prototyping project by an e.quinox committee, exploring portable engineered solutions for off-grid Rwandan households. Its focus on parts that travel easily resurfaces in Project Amazi.
description2: Like every e.quinox project, Truckle was prototyped at Imperial by a student team and taken to Rwanda for field testing.
outcomes: Prototype designed, built and field-tested by an Imperial student team

title: Mushroom Farming Research
imageAlt: Mushroom farming research in Rwanda, an earlier e.quinox project
description: An earlier e.quinox research project investigating mushroom farming alongside the energy work in rural Rwanda, looking at protein, income and nutrient cycling at the household scale.
description2: The research informed the committee's thinking on how engineered infrastructure can open up agricultural opportunity.
outcomes: Insights on income and nutrition recorded
